name: Vitamin B12- and Folate-Independent Constitutional Megaloblastic Anemia
aliases: Constitutional Megaloblastic Anemia without Vitamin B12 or Folate Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Vitamin B12- and Folate-Independent Constitutional Megaloblastic Anemia

criteria.description: Presence of megaloblastic anemia confirmed by bone marrow examination showing megaloblastic erythropoiesis
Normal serum vitamin B12 and folate levels excluding nutritional deficiency
Exclusion of other causes of megaloblastic anemia including drug-induced and acquired causes
Positive family history suggesting inherited pattern
Persistent macrocytosis on peripheral blood smear

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of megaloblastic anemia with normal vitamin B12 and folate levels and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and hematological after ruling out nutritional and acquired causes.

searchTerms: large immature red blood cells in marrow

pathognomonic.symptomName: Macrocytic anemia with elevated mean corpuscular volume
searchTerms: anemia with large red blood cells
pale skin from low red blood cells
skin looks lighter due to anemia

common.symptomName: Mild jaundice secondary to ineffective erythropoiesis
searchTerms: mild jaundice from poor red cell production
slight yellowing due to ineffective erythropoiesis
fatigue related to low red blood cells

rare.symptomName: Neurological manifestations such as peripheral neuropathy
Cardiovascular complications secondary to chronic anemia
searchTerms: heart problems caused by chronic anemia
cardiovascular issues from low red blood cells
recurrent infections due to immune weakness
infections caused by low white blood cells

laboratory: Bone marrow biopsy showing megaloblastic erythropoiesis
Normal serum vitamin B12 and folate levels
genetic: Potential autosomal recessive inheritance pattern suggested by family history
other: Exclusion of nutritional, drug-induced, and acquired causes essential

distinguishingFeatures: History of exposure to drugs like methotrexate or phenytoin

redFlags: Severe pancytopenia with risk of bleeding or infection
Failure to respond to vitamin B12 and folate supplementation
